text:
Inter Miami’s quest to defend their MLS Cup title is over.
The South Florida side had two gilt-edged chances to take the lead in Game 2 of their best-of-three first-round series against Columbus in the MLS Playoffs on Friday, but missed both of them along with several others, later succumbing to a terrific stoppage-time winner from Santi Rodríguez in a 1-0 win for the Crew.
The Crew’s win followed a 3-0 domination of Miami away from home at Nu Stadium, a game in which Miami defender Gonzalo Luján was issued a red card in the 36th minute. Miami’s status as MLS’s best team away from home gave them plenty of hope going into the all-important matchup in Ohio. The chances came – for Messi in the 14th minute, and a point-blank effort from Germán Berterame in the 84th that went over the bar – but the goals didn’t.
Instead, Rodríguez’s strike saw the Crew move on to the delight of a raucous home crowd in cold, rainy conditions. They will face the winner of the New England Revolution and Philadelphia Union’s matchup, with the Revs currently up 1-0 on Philly, who are hosting Game 2.
For Columbus, the result is the latest in a stunning rise from dead last in the Eastern Conference earlier this year, a start that cost head coach Henrik Rydström his job halfway through. The Crew have been on fire under interim head coach Laurent Courtois, winning eight of their final nine games to sneak into the playoffs and now two straight against the defending champions. The September acquisition of Rodríguez has been a big part of that turnaround, with the Uruguayan scoring three times and adding eight assists in the regular season.
For Miami, the focus in the aftermath a playoff exit will have global resonance thanks to Messi, who turned 39 over the summer and has already retired internationally for Argentina. This year has been a trying one for the Argentine, with his father, Jorge, suffering from a serious illness throughout the World Cup, and dying weeks after the final that Argentina lost, 1-0, to Spain.
Jorge Messi was deeply involved in his son’s footballing career, acting as his agent and closest confidant throughout.
“I wanted to win [the World Cup] to bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn’t; my legs wouldn’t give any more,” Messi wrote in an open letter to his father after his passing. “I have only played football and now I have quite a few doubts about whether I’ll keep doing it for much longer.”
Messi announced his international retirement from Argentina not long after. He has not, however, indicated publicly in any way that he plans to end his playing career altogether.
Messi signed a contract extension with Miami through the 2028 MLS season late last year, but it’s unknown how the league’s change to a fall-to-spring calendar, confirmed weeks after Messi put pen to paper, will affect the deal. Regardless, Messi would be far from the first player to retire in the middle of a recently signed extension. Jordi Alba signed an extension with Miami midway through the 2025 MLS season, only to retire after winning MLS Cup last year.
If Friday’s game was Messi’s last as a professional, it will count as a disappointing one for reasons beyond the result. The Argentine was unable to produce the moments of magic that have defined so much of his career, often swarmed by Columbus defenders when he got the ball and harried by them off of it. He was responsible for one of the two biggest missed chances of the match for Miami, doing well to bring down a lofted ball within the six-yard box but firing uncharacteristically wide past the far post in the 14th minute.
Should he choose to keep playing, he’ll have plenty of reason: Miami’s regular season has earned them a spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup, one of vanishingly few trophies he has not won at the clubs he’s played for.
digest_he: חלומותיה של אינטר מיאמי להגן על תואר אליפות ה-MLS הסתיימו לאחר הפסד 1-0 לקולומבוס קרו במשחק השני בסדרת הסיבוב הראשון. למרות הזדמנויות רבות שאליהן הגיעו השחקנים ובהם ליאו מסי, שער מאוחר של סנטיאגו רודריגז בתוספת הזמן הכריע את ההתמודדות והשלים ניצחון מצטבר לקולומבוס. עבור מיאמי מדובר בסיום אכזב לעונה שעמדה בצל אתגרים אישיים של מסי, הכוללים את פרישתו הבינלאומית ופטירתו של אביו. קולומבוס ממשיכה לשלב הבא במסע המרשים שלה תחת המאמן הזמני לורן קורטואה, ותפגוש את המנצחת בין ניו אינגלנד רבולושן לפילדלפיה יוניון.
